title: Part Two: Logotherapy in a Nutshell
coreMove: Translate emptiness into a concrete responsibility through work, love, or attitude instead of chasing mood relief.
sourcePressure: The theory unit presents logotherapy, the will to meaning, the existential vacuum, noogenic neurosis, three routes to meaning, paradoxical intention, and dereflection.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Do not reduce logotherapy to passion, happiness, or self-help purpose statements. It is about being addressed by a specific responsibility, especially when pleasure and power cannot answer the emptiness.

sourceAnchors.name: logotherapy
sourceAnchors.detail: The frozen source identifies Part Two as the section where Frankl explains logotherapy.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Logotherapy should enter as a discipline of responsibility, not a promise of better mood.

sourceAnchors.name: existential vacuum
sourceAnchors.detail: The source says the existential vacuum names a modern emptiness problem.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The vacuum is not solved by noise; it is answered by a task with a claim on you.

sourceAnchors.name: paradoxical intention
sourceAnchors.detail: The source notes paradoxical intention as one therapeutic method in the framework.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Paradoxical intention can appear as the strange moment when fighting the symptom directly gives it more power.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: retired civil engineer whose first year after work is filled with errands and television but no claim on his skill
exampleSpecs.audience: a retiree who is comfortable and still increasingly hollow
exampleSpecs.stakes: pleasure and free time are not answering the empty mornings
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he opens a box of old bridge inspection notes and agrees to mentor a town culvert committee for six weeks, turning skill into service
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The garage shelf holds three binders of bridge inspections nobody has asked about in a year.

exampleSpecs.domain: pediatric speech clinic aide bored by repetitive articulation cards until a child points to one sound she needs for her own name
exampleSpecs.audience: a clinic aide who has been treating the work as dull compliance
exampleSpecs.stakes: meaning appears when the exercise becomes a responsibility to one child, not when the task becomes glamorous
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she writes the child's name above the sound deck and slows the drill because the work now has a face
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The laminated card squeaks under the dry-erase marker.

exampleSpecs.domain: software quality analyst caught in an existential vacuum after promotion removes hands-on craft
exampleSpecs.audience: a promoted analyst with status, salary, and no daily responsibility that feels real
exampleSpecs.stakes: the promotion offers power but strips away the work that carried meaning
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he declines one status meeting and takes ownership of a recurring accessibility defect until the screen reader flow actually works
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What if the promotion gave him power and removed the work that made him answerable?

exampleSpecs.domain: widower learning that love can still organize action after the beloved person is gone
exampleSpecs.audience: a man resisting the idea that love has any task left after death
exampleSpecs.stakes: memory can become either shrine maintenance or a responsibility to keep a promise alive
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: you see him move one recipe card from the memory box to the counter and cook the soup his wife made for neighbors after surgery
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You see the recipe card before you see the photograph.

exampleSpecs.domain: stand-up trainee with crippling stage anxiety using paradoxical intention in a small open mic
exampleSpecs.audience: a performer whose fear of shaking makes the shaking worse
exampleSpecs.stakes: fighting the symptom directly keeps feeding it
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coach tells her to begin by deliberately showing the audience her shaking hand, and the prediction is whether the tremor grows or loses command
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Try to make the tremor obvious in the first ten seconds," the coach says.

exampleSpecs.domain: university advising office where a student has every option open and feels emptier each week
exampleSpecs.audience: an advisor helping a student move from abstract choice to one concrete responsibility
exampleSpecs.stakes: limitless options are becoming paralysis rather than freedom
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after three meetings of preference lists, the advisor asks whom the next semester of study would serve and circles one practicum tied to that answer
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Thomas three advising appointments to admit that every open door felt weightless.

skillTargets: distinguish will to meaning from pleasure or power
diagnose existential vacuum in concrete behavior
choose work love or attitude as a route to responsibility
apply paradoxical intention without making it a gimmick

tryThisNowSpec: Name one empty routine from today and add the person, task, or unavoidable fact that could make the next version a responsibility.
